Petition under Sections 17(3) & 17(4) of Electricity Act, 2003 seeking approval for creation of security interest over all of the Petitioner’s Assets in favour of Respondent No. 2 as the Security Trustee acting for the benefit of the Lender in respect of the Petitioner’s transmission project.

2. The Petitioner has filed the present Petition under Section 17 of the Act seeking approval for the creation of security interest over its movable and immovable assets in favour of Respondent No. 2, Catalyst Trusteeship Limited (hereinafter referred to as the "Security Trustee"), acting for and on behalf of and for the benefit of Respondent Nos. 1 i.e., Axis Bank Limited (hereinafter referred to as the "Lender"), including their subsequent transferees, assigns, novatees and any refinancing lenders to the Project, pursuant to the Security Trustee Agreement, Facility Agreement and other financing documents executed in connection with the Project. The Petitioner has made the following prayers:

_“(a) Approve the creation of Security Interest by way of hypothecation/mortgage/ charge/pledge/assignment (as applicable), over the assets listed at Paragraph 20 above, and all the movable and immovable assets, accounts, Project Documents (including assignment of transmission licence) etc., both present and future, of Petitioner in terms of the Financing Documents, or as may be agreed between the Petitioner and the Lender from time to time, in favour of Lender/Security Trustee to secure the financial assistance availed/to be availed from the Lender and its subsequent transferees, assigns, novatees and substitutes thereof and any refinancing lenders to the Project, by executing deed of hypothecation and power of attorney in relation thereto, Indenture of Mortgage, Mortgage by deposit of title_

_(b) Pass such other orders that this Commission deems fit in the facts and circumstances of this case.”_

5. The Petitioner has submitted that pursuant to the terms of the Facility Agreement, it is required to create security interest in favour of Catalyst Trusteeship Limited, _inter alia,_ as follows:

- (a) all the rights, title, interest, benefits, claim, and demands whatsoever of the Borrower in the Project Documents, duly acknowledged and consented to by the relevant counter-parties to such Project Documents and subject to the terms of such Project Documents;

6. The Petitioner has submitted that, as per Article 15.2.2 of the TSA, it is entitled to create any encumbrance over all or part of the receivables or the Transmission Project Assets in favour of the lender(s) or lenders’ representative (as defined in the TSA) as security for amounts payable under the Financing Agreements. Therefore, the Petitioner has the full right to create a security interest and charge in favour of Catalyst Trusteeship Limited for the benefit of the lenders, subject to conditions prescribed under Article 15 of the TSA.

9. The Petition was listed for hearing on 30.4.2026. When the matter was called, none appeared on behalf of the Petitioner. However, upon noting that the present Petition seeks approval for the creation of a security interest over the assets of the Petitioner, the notice was issued in the matter.

10. Vide Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as "RoP") dated 30.4.2026, the Petitioner was directed to implead Adani Renewable Energy Park Rajasthan Limited (hereinafter referred to as "AREPRL") as a party to the present Petition, file a revised Memo of Parties, and furnish the information sought by the Commission vide letter dated 12.1.2026. Further, the Respondents were granted the opportunity to file their respective replies.

11. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that, in compliance with the directions issued vide RoP dated 30.4.2026, the Petitioner has filed

a revised memo of parties vide affidavit dated 1.6.2026. It was further submitted that the information sought by the Commission vide its letter dated 12.1.2026 has also been furnished.

12. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has filed a compliance affidavit dated 1.6.2026, furnishing the information sought vide the previous RoPs. It was further submitted that, by affidavit dated 17.6.2026, the Petitioner has placed on record the “No Due Certificates” issued by the lenders, evidencing repayment of the loan facilities availed by it. Accordingly, learned counsel for the Petitioner prayed that the matter be reserved for orders.

17. The Petitioner has submitted that it is permitted to create encumbrances over

- _i. the Lenders or the Lenders' Representative on their behalf shall have entered into the Financing Agreements and agreed in writing to the provisions of this Agreement; and_

_“17. (3) No licensee shall any time assign his licence or transfer his utility, or any part hereof, by sale, lease, exchange or otherwise without the prior approval of the Appropriate Commission._

19. The Petitioner and the Lender have appointed Catalyst Trusteeship Limited as the Security Trustee for the creation of a Security Interest over all the movable and immovable assets of the Project. In our view, Catalyst Trusteeship Limited needs to be given comfort for the creation of security for the benefit of the Lender, as security for the financial assistance provided by them. We, therefore, accord approval allowing the Petitioner to create a Security Interest in favour of Catalyst Trusteeship Limited, acting as the Security Trustee for and on behalf of the Lender, including their subsequent transferees, assigns, novatees and any refinancing lenders to the Project, by way of mortgage or any other security document over the Project assets through execution of the Indenture of Mortgage and other financing documents relating to the Project. The Petitioner is directed to submit a signed copy of the Indenture of Mortgage for the Project immediately after its execution.

Carbon Resources Private Limited

**Coram: Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member**

The Petitioner, Carbon Resources Private Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the Applicant”), is a Private Limited Company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 on 4.9.1991, has made the present Application under Section 14 read with Section 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) read with Regulation 6 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for the Grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as “the Trading Licence Regulations”), amended from

2. In accordance with sub-section (2) of Section 15 of the Act read with Clause (4) of Regulation 6 of the Trading Licence Regulations, notices were published by the Petitioner on 10.4.2026 in all India edition of the ‘Business Standard’ (Kolkata, Chennai, New Delhi, Lucknow, and Mumbai), ‘Financial Express’ (New Delhi, Chennai/Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow), ‘The North East Times’ (Guwahati) and ‘The Assam Rising’ (Guwahati).  The Petitioner has submitted that no objections have been received in response to the public notices.

4. On the above consideration, the Commission, vide its order dated 7.7.2026, had proposed to grant a Category 'III' inter-State trading licence to the Petitioner. The relevant portions of the said order dated 7.7.2026 are extracted as under:

- _“18. In accordance with Clause (2) of Regulation 3 of the Trading Licence Regulations, the Petitioner should have at least one full-time professional possessing qualifications and experience in power system operation and the_

_19. On consideration of the above facts, after a preliminary examination, we find that the Petitioner meets the requirements as specified in the Trading Licence Regulations for the grant of a Category 'III' trading licence. In view thereof, the Commission proposes to grant a Category 'III' trading licence to the Petitioner. We direct that a notice under Clause (a) of Sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act be issued inviting further suggestions or objections to the proposal of the Commission.”_

5. In line with the above-mentioned order dated 7.7.2026, notice under Clause (a) of Sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act was published in all editions of the Hindustan Times (English) and Dainik Bhaskar (Hindi) on 10.7.2026. No suggestions or objections have been received in response to the Commission’s notice.

6. The case was called out for the hearing on 30.7.2026. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that no objection had been received in response to the public notice published by the Commission under subSection (5) of Section 15 of the Act. He further submitted that the Petitioner’s company would comply with the requirements specified in the Trading Licence Regulations during the subsistence of the trading licence, i.e., for 25 years, if granted.

7.      Clause (9) of Regulation 6 of the Trading Licence Regulations provides as under:

_“(9) On consideration of further objections or suggestions received and the reply of the applicant thereto, if any, the Commission may grant the licence or reject the application, for reasons to be recorded in writing if the application does not confirm to the provisions of the Act, the rules or regulations or provisions of any other law for the time being in force:_

_Provided that no application shall be rejected, unless the applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard.”_

8. On consideration of the materials on record, we are satisfied that the Petitioner company meets the requirements of the Act and the Trading Licence Regulations for the grant of an inter-State trading licence for Category 'III'.

9. The grant of the trading licence to the Petitioner (hereinafter referred to as “the licensee”) is subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions throughout the period of subsistence of the licence:

- (a) The licensee shall comply with the provisions of the Act, the Rules, and the Regulations, particularly Trading Licence Regulations, orders, and directions issued by the Commission, from time to time, and any other law in force;

- (b) The licensee shall comply with orders and directions issued by the Commission from time to time;

(f) The licensee shall continue to be governed by the qualifications and disqualifications specified in Chapter 2 of the Trading Licence Regulations during the subsistence of the licence;

(g) The licensee shall continue to abide by the terms and conditions of the licence specified in Chapter V of the Trading Licence Regulations, as amended from time to time;

(i) Non-compliance with the provisions of the Act, Rules, Regulations, and the provisions of the Trading Licence Regulations shall make the licence of the Petitioner liable for revocation;

(j) If the licensee fails to undertake trading in electricity within a year from the date of the licence, the licence shall be liable for revocation in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the Trading Licence Regulations; and

10. An extract of a copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (the Ministry of Power) and the Central Electricity Authority in terms of sub-Section (7) of Section 15 of the Act for their information and record.
